display.purpose: The page title only. One per page.

headline.purpose: Report headline insight, drill prompt, card titles.

title.purpose: Buttons, tabs, table captions, the play status line.

label.purpose: Verdict badges, field labels, secondary status.

notation.purpose: SAN moves, clocks, eval numbers, best lines. Tabular figures.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: Every panel at rest. Warm, not black, so it does not read as dirt on cream.

shadows.name: card-raised
shadows.purpose: Hover on an interactive card, and anything temporarily above the page.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every interactive element. Never removed without a replacement.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, and color state changes on controls.

motion.name: duration-instrument
motion.purpose: The eval bar's fill height, so the swing is legible rather than instant.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action that advances the task in a region: Analyze, Load, New game.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: 600 1rem/1.4 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); background: var(--felt, #3f5f4a); color: var(--page, #faf6f0); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--r-md, 8px); padding: 8px 16px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--felt-deep, #334e3c); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(63,95,74,0.28); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: var(--felt-deep, #334e3c); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Every action that is not the primary one. Stays visible when disabled.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font: 600 1rem/1.4 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); background: var(--surface, #fff); color: var(--ink, #23201c); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #e3d9cc); border-radius: var(--r-md, 8px); padding: 8px 16px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--felt-wash, #e7ede9); color: var(--felt-deep, #334e3c); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(63,95,74,0.28); } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { color: var(--ink-faint, #9a9086); cursor: default; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Sunken well on paper. Says type here without a shadow.
components.css: .ds-input { font: 400 0.95rem/1.55 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); background: var(--surface-sunken, #f3ece2); color: var(--ink, #23201c); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #e3d9cc); border-radius: var(--r-md, 8px); padding: 8px 12px; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-faint, #9a9086); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--felt, #3f5f4a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(63,95,74,0.28); }

components.name: Tab Bar
components.description: Two tabs, always both visible. The active one joins the card below it.
components.html: <nav class="ds-tabs"><button class="ds-tab ds-tab-active">Play the engine</button><button class="ds-tab">Analyze & drills</button></nav>
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline, #e3d9cc); } .ds-tab { font: 600 1rem/1.4 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px 8px 0 0; color: var(--ink-muted, #6b6259); padding: 8px 16px; margin-bottom: -1px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-tab:hover:not(.ds-tab-active) { background: var(--felt-wash, #e7ede9); color: var(--ink, #23201c); } .ds-tab-active { background: var(--surface, #fff); color: var(--ink, #23201c); border-bottom-color: var(--felt, #3f5f4a); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(63,95,74,0.28); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Every functional region. Shadow is the edge; no border.
components.html:
You hung a piece three times

Most of your losses start with a piece left undefended in the middlegame.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface, #fff); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px); padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(35,32,28,0.04), 0 2px 8px rgba(35,32,28,0.06); } .ds-card-title { font: 650 1.15rem/1.3 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--ink, #23201c); margin: 0 0 8px; } .ds-card-body { font: 400 0.95rem/1.55 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); color: var(--ink, #23201c); margin: 0; max-width: 70ch; }

components.name: Move Row with Verdict Badge
components.description: The dense scanned region. Only mistakes are badged; good moves stay silent.
components.html:
1. Nf3
  2. Qh5 blunder -4.2
  3. Nc6 inaccuracy -0.6
components.css: .ds-moves { list-style: decimal; padding-left: 32px; margin: 0; font: 400 0.95rem/1.4 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-moves li { padding: 2px 4px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 4px); border-left: 2px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; } .ds-moves li:hover { background: var(--felt-wash, #e7ede9); } .ds-move-active { background: var(--felt-wash, #e7ede9); border-left-color: var(--felt, #3f5f4a); } .ds-san { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-weight: 500; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-verdict { font: 600 0.8rem/1.2 var(--font-sans, 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif); letter-spacing: 0.02em; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 4px); padding: 1px 4px; } .ds-verdict-inaccuracy { color: #8f6200; } .ds-verdict-mistake { color: #c2410c; } .ds-verdict-blunder { color: #b3261e; }

components.name: Eval Bar
components.description: The board's instrument. Wears the board's colors, never the UI's.
components.css: .ds-evalbar { width: 14px; height: 200px; background: var(--board-dark, #b58863); border-radius: var(--r-md, 8px); position: relative; overflow: hidden; } .ds-evalfill { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 62%; background: var(--board-light, #f0d9b5); transition: height 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); }

components.name: Clock
components.description: Tabular figures so the layout never reflows as it ticks.
components.css: .ds-clock { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 1.4rem; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink, #23201c); text-align: right; padding: 2px 6px; }

narrative.overview:
Chess Coach looks like the table you sit down at after a game, not like an analytics product. The board is the classic wooden one every club and every online lobby already uses, so a beginner recognises it before they read a word. Around it, the room is warm paper (#faf6f0), and the only voice that belongs to the software is the green of table felt (#3f5f4a). Nothing shouts. The visitor has just lost a game and arrived slightly embarrassed; a loud interface would make that worse.

The system is warm, quiet, and dense with real information. Panels are white cards that sit on the paper with a soft shadow, because the visitor is working with several distinct objects at once: a board, a move list, an explanation, a graph, a drill. Cards make those objects separable at a glance without borders everywhere. Typography is a single humanist sans (Inter) doing all the talking, with monospace reserved for the things that are literally notation: moves, clocks, evaluations.

Color is rationed hard. The felt marks structure and engine truth. A separate, saturated verdict scale (green through red) marks how good a move was, and it appears only on move quality. Those two families never trade jobs. Rejected outright: a dark analytics chrome, neon accents, the arbitrary blue that used to sit on the active tab, and any decorative gradient or glassmorphism.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper page, white cards, wooden board, green felt accent.
One typeface family; monospace only for real notation.
Verdict color is earned by the engine, never used for decoration.
Soft, warm, low-contrast shadows; no hard borders doing a card's job.
Generous line height and muted secondary text, because beginners read every word.

rules.name: The Felt Never Judges Rule
rules.body: Table Felt and the verdict scale are separate vocabularies. Felt marks where you are and what the engine is showing; verdict color marks how good a move was. A green button is a bug. A felt-colored blunder badge is a bug. Audit test: cover the board and ask of every colored element, "is this navigation, or is this a grade?"

rules.name: The Rationed Accent Rule
rules.body: Felt covers less than 10% of any screen. If two felt elements compete for attention in the same region, one of them is decoration and should be neutral.

rules.name: The Board Owns The Wood Rule
rules.body: Board Light and Board Dark appear on the board and the eval bar, and nowhere else. Extending the wood into the chrome turns the room into a theme.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Anything that counts or changes in place (clocks, evaluation numbers, move indices, drill progress) uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. A clock that reflows every second is a defect.

rules.name: The Notation Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for SAN, FEN, clocks, and eval values. Never for headings, buttons, or body prose.

rules.name: The Board Never Shrinks Below Its Squares Rule
rules.body: The board keeps a 1:1 aspect ratio and never drops below 280px. If the viewport cannot hold the board and the side column, the side column moves below the board; it never squeezes the board.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows use rgba(35,32,28,...), never rgba(0,0,0,...). Pure black shadows on cream read as dirt.

rules.name: The One Elevation Step Rule
rules.body: A card is either resting or raised. There is no third level; stacking more shadow to signal more importance is how a layout stops having a hierarchy.

dos: Do keep Table Felt (#3f5f4a) under 10% of any screen, on navigation state, primary actions, focus, and the eval line only.
Do use the verdict scale (#1d7a44 / #8f6200 / #c2410c / #b3261e) exclusively for move quality, in both the move list and the eval graph, so the two always agree.
Do use tabular-nums on every clock, evaluation, and counter.
Do cap explanation prose at 65-75ch, since the explanation is the product.
Do give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible ring (0 0 0 3px rgba(63,95,74,0.28)).
Do keep the board at 1:1 and let the side column move below it on narrow screens.
donts: Don't paint UI chrome in the board's wood (#f0d9b5 / #b58863). The board owns those.
Don't reintroduce the old blue (#4a86e8) or add any second accent.
Don't combine a border and a shadow on the same element.
Don't use pure black (#000) for text or shadows; the room is warm.
Don't badge good moves. Only inaccuracy, mistake, and blunder earn a badge.
Don't use monospace for headings, buttons, or prose.
Don't hide a disabled control. It stays visible so the visitor learns the flow.
